meta.purpose: Master 3-paper target_cells plan for BPSC Bihar Special I/II/III (450 questions total, 150 each). Derived from the existing live-taxonomy check (Step 0) -- NOT a fresh invented scheme.
meta.source_of_topic_split: Live public.distribution_config.sub_topic_weights['Bihar-Specific'] and its source data pyq-analysis/summary_3_subtopic_within_subject.csv / combined_dataset.csv (141 raw PYQ-tagged Bihar-Specific rows across 66th re-71st).
meta.topics_note: These are the ONLY 5 sub_topic values that exist anywhere in the PYQ-tagged dataset for Bihar-Specific -- not a rollup of a finer scheme. Matches AdminApp.jsx's SUBTOPICS_BY_SUBJECT['Bihar-Specific'] and the live distribution_config keys exactly, so drafted content stays weighted-generator-compatible.
meta.type_weights_basis: Live distribution_config.question_type_weights['Bihar-Specific'] (mcq 95.97%, statement_based 1.61%, match_the_following 2.42%) -- this already excludes the 69th cycle as a confirmed outlier, per the same adjustment applied to every subject during the original config push. Non-mcq questions are allocated only to (topic, difficulty) cells that actually showed that format in the raw PYQ data -- no invented format diversity where the real exam shows none.
meta.difficulty_note: 5/141 raw PYQ questions (3.5%) were easy -- Bihar-Specific skews far harder than History. Recent Developments and Polity & Governance show ZERO easy questions anywhere in the raw 6-cycle sample; both start at 'medium'.
meta.allocation_method: Largest-remainder rounding: subject-total -> per-topic (proportional to raw PYQ frequency) -> per-difficulty within topic (proportional to raw frequency) -> non-mcq types layered onto the (topic,difficulty) cells that had real precedent, remainder mcq. Then each cell split 3 ways for papers I/II/III via a greedy balancer (assigns each cell's leftover units to whichever paper currently has the lowest running total) so every paper lands on exactly 150 and the 3 papers sum back to the master cells exactly.

user_category_mapping.note: The task's originally-sketched 8-category list (History/Geography/Economy/Polity & Panchayati Raj/Culture-Arts-Literature-Festivals/Govt Schemes(static)/Personalities/Static GK-Misc) does not exist as a separate live taxonomy -- it doesn't override the 5-bucket empirical one. These richer categories are real content THEMES, not new topic values; they live inside concept_group_id + question body, same way History carried 'Sher Shah's tomb' inside the 'Medieval' topic rather than inventing a 'Monuments' topic.
user_category_mapping.Bihar Culture/Arts/Literature/Festivals: History & Culture (bundled with History in the real PYQ tagging, not separate)
user_category_mapping.Important Bihar Personalities: History & Culture, mostly (freedom fighters, historical rulers) -- a few modern-era figures may fit Recent Developments if the question is about a living/recent figure's current role
user_category_mapping.Bihar Static GK/Misc (districts, rivers,: Geography, mostly (rivers/parks/physical facts); a handful of administrative-division facts could sit in Polity & Governance
user_category_mapping.Bihar Government Schemes (static, long-r: Recent Developments (this is where the raw PYQ data's scheme/programme questions actually landed)

known_gaps.economy_durable_content_shortage: Discovered while sourcing Paper I: the Bihar Special Orange Book's Economy chapter (14 pages) is dominated by year-specific Economic Survey/budget statistics that are current-affairs-shaped and explicitly excluded from this paper by design (see Step 1). Cross-checked against the REAL 70th/71st BPSC papers' own Bihar-Specific/Economy questions (25 across all 6 cycles tagged) -- same pattern holds there too: the overwhelming majority are tied to a specific year's survey number. This is not a property of one thin source; it appears to be how BPSC itself tests this sub-topic. Only ~13 genuinely durable, non-perishable facts were identified for Paper I (institutional-establishment years, named-policy structures, structural/analytical insights like the Freight Equalization Policy's deindustrialization effect or migration-remittance as a consumption driver) -- against an original per-paper target of 27.
known_gaps.what_this_means_for_paper_1: Paper I's Economy target_cells reduced from 27 to 13 (confirmed, see paper_1 below); the freed 14 slots were reallocated to Geography (+5, using already-drafted surplus from the Batch 02 reserve file) and History & Culture (+9, newly drafted) -- both topics had clean, verified surplus at the needed difficulty levels.
known_gaps.what_this_means_for_papers_2_and_3: NOT yet resolved. paper_2 and paper_3 below still show their ORIGINAL, pre-rebalance Economy/Geography/History & Culture numbers (Economy ~26 each) -- these are known to rest on the same flawed assumption Paper I's did, and should NOT be treated as reliable. Expect the same rebalancing exercise (or better) when Papers II/III are actually sourced and drafted, unless better source material arrives first specifically covering: land-reform implementation outcomes (not just the Zamindari Abolition Act's existence, which is already used under History & Culture), Five-Year-Plan-era Bihar industrial history, or banking/cooperative-credit history. Do not silently draft Papers II/III's Economy sections at their currently-stated volume without re-checking source depth first.
known_gaps.master_450_note: master_450 below has been updated to reflect Paper I's confirmed change (Economy -14, Geography +5, History & Culture +9) so the grand total still correctly sums to 450, but the portion of that total sitting in paper_2/paper_3 is exactly as uncertain as described above -- the master total is arithmetically consistent, not independently verified for papers 2 and 3.
